$comment: Throne and Liberty event schedule. Captured from questlog.gg's event calendar on
This is DETERMINISTIC DATA, not a live feed. The calendar renders a fixed weekly grid:
a region selector, a UTC offset, and the same daily time slots repeating. There is no
spawn API to poll — reports are that Amazon never exposed one. So the timer computes
everything locally from this table plus the player's region and timezone, which is more
reliable than any scraper and has no runtime dependency on a third-party site.
Maintenance: this needs a refresh when a patch changes the rotation. It is a data file
edit, not a code change — that is the point of shipping it as JSON.
STATUS: time slots and event types are CONFIRMED from the live calendar. The specific
boss assigned to each Field Boss slot per weekday is NOT yet captured — see
`bossRotation` below. The timer is useful without it (it can say 'Field Bosses in 18
minutes'); naming the boss is a refinement.
$scheduleShapeIsWrong: THE dailySlots MODEL BELOW CANNOT EXPRESS THE REAL SCHEDULE. Captured from a live client
2026-08-04 (process TL, 1.443.22.7936), the in-game map's Daily tab shows:
So slots are PER WEEKDAY, not per day: Thursday and Monday are empty, Sunday runs SIEGE at
18:00 (confirmed by a player — it is scheduled guild PvP, not a boss, so it must not be
labelled 'Field Bosses'), and the rest run 17:00 and 20:00. The number of bosses per slot
varies too — some slots show one icon, others five.
A flat dailySlots list repeated every day is therefore wrong in three separate ways. This
needs reshaping to weekday -> slots before the timer can be trusted.
Also note these client times (17:00/20:00) DO NOT MATCH questlog's Americas grid (19:00/
22:00). The client is authoritative for the player's own server; see $timezoneWarning.
$iconIndex: The map's Content Settings window lists EVERY boss next to its icon WITH ITS NAME IN TEXT —
roughly 38 bosses (most in normal and 'Ascended' form), 9 archbosses including Ramux, and 6
boonstones. That single screen is a complete icon->name index, and capturing it once solves
the schedule's icon problem the same way the named-currency reference solves the currency
bar's. Prompt for it on first run.
Each entry has a checkbox. A boss the player has unticked does not appear on their schedule
at all, so the index doubles as the filter state and both are worth reading.
Consequence: the fieldBosses roster below (seven entries, from getFieldBossEntries) is badly
incomplete and should not be built on.
$regionCoverage: questlog only has real boss data for EUROPE. Confirmed 2026-08-04 by a player of the game,
and consistent with what the calendar renders: Europe shows named T3/T2 pairs per slot,
while Americas shows only generic 'Field Bosses' markers and Asia shows nothing.
So the Americas entries below are NOT a captured boss rotation — they are questlog's generic
event markers. Do not present them as a boss schedule, and do not wait for questlog to fill
in NA or Asia; the data is not there to scrape.
THE REAL SOURCE FOR NA AND ASIA IS THE PLAYER'S OWN CLIENT. The in-game map lists the day's
bosses and spawn times down the left side, per-server accurate by definition, for every
region including the ones no external site covers. That makes it a user-initiated capture —
the same pattern already used for the Combat Power tooltip and the named-currency reference,
and something this app can already do. See docs/boss-timer.md, which reached this conclusion
before the region gap was confirmed.
$timeModel: HOW TIMES ARE STORED, AND WHY NOT IN UTC.
Each region's slots are WALL-CLOCK TIMES plus a named timeZone (defaultTimeZone). BossSchedule
converts them to a real instant at read time and everything downstream — countdown, alerts,
the overlay — works in instants and renders in the USER'S OWN local timezone. So the pipeline
already is 'schedule -> absolute instant -> viewer's clock'; the only thing not stored in UTC
Storing the table as UTC would be actively worse IF the game schedules by Pacific wall clock:
17:00 Pacific is 00:00 UTC in summer and 01:00 UTC in winter, so a UTC table would be an hour
wrong for half the year and would need re-capturing twice annually. Wall clock plus a zone
OPEN QUESTION, and it decides which model is right: does the in-game schedule shift with US
daylight saving, or is it pinned to a fixed offset? The client renders times in the VIEWER'S
local timezone (confirmed: a Pacific player sees 17:00/20:00), which does not by itself reveal
what the underlying schedule is anchored to. Check the same slot before and after a DST
boundary: if the local hour holds, wall-clock storage is correct and nothing changes. If it
moves by an hour, the schedule is UTC-anchored and this table must be converted to UTC.
$timezoneWarning: UNRESOLVED, AND IT INVALIDATES EVERY HOUR IN THIS FILE IF WRONG.
questlog's calendar renders a 'UTC -07:00' header, which is the VIEWER'S timezone, not the
server's. So the hour values captured from that page may already be converted into the
capturing machine's local time rather than being server-local wall clock. Both the Americas
and Europe slots here were read off that page from a UTC-07:00 machine.
If they are viewer-local, every entry is offset by the difference between UTC-07:00 and the
player's server timezone — for Europe that is around nine hours, which would make the

$source: weeklySlots is CAPTURED FROM A LIVE CLIENT (2026-08-04) and is the authoritative one.
dailySlots below it is the older questlog-derived guess, kept only so the difference is
visible: questlog claims field bosses at 19:00/22:00, the client shows 17:00/20:00.
weeklySlots wins wherever both are present.
SIEGE IS WEEKLY -- 18:00 every Sunday, same time, corrected 2026-08-06 by the product owner.
An earlier pass read 16/08 Sun as an empty row in the Daily panel and concluded biweekly. That
was a misread, and it was published. The everyDays/since machinery it motivated is kept because
it is tested and harmless, but nothing in this file uses it any more.
THE DAILY TAB IS ONLY SIEGE AND ARCHBOSSES. Regular field bosses -- Talus, Excavator-9 and the
rest -- live on the HOURLY tab, are always running, and rotate. So on a day with archbosses BOTH
streams are live at once, and this file currently models only one of them. The hourly stream
stays generic Field Bosses; the archboss slots are the named ones.
Field bosses ARE weekly, re-confirmed over the same 21 days: 17:00 and 20:00 on Tue, Wed, Fri
and Sat; Thursday and Monday carry nothing at all. Slot COMPOSITION rotates (one boss at 17:00
and five at 20:00 one week, inverted the next) but the times do not, and the timer needs only
the times.
The panel is explicitly labelled LOCAL TIME in the client, which is why slot times are read in
the player's own zone and the server timezone setting was removed.
BOSS NAMES: each slot takes an optional "bosses" array, because ONE slot can hold several
bosses at the same time — the client shows one icon at 17:00 and five at 20:00. With names the
overlay reads "20:00 - Ahzreil, Talus, Grand Aelon"; with the array absent or empty it falls
back to "Field Bosses", which is true rather than a guess. Never put a name here that has not
been read off the client: a plausible wrong boss sends the player across the map for nothing.
The names come from the map's Content Settings window, which lists every boss beside its icon
in text. That is a one-time user capture; the schedule icons are unlabelled on their own.
=== HOURLY STREAM, read from the client 2026-08-06 (Hourly tab, PST) ===
Seven slots a day, and the list starts at 08:00 with nothing above it:
11:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
14:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
18:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
18:30  1 boss        GUILD PvP
21:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
21:30  1 boss        GUILD PvP
23:00  2 bosses      peace, rotating
The two guild slots are at fixed times every day -- 18:30 and 21:30 -- and are the only
single-event slots. The peace slots rotate randomly through the regular boss roster (Talus,
Excavator-9 and the rest), so they must stay generic Field Boss: naming a rotating slot would be
wrong most days, and wrong confidently.
NOT YET MODELLED. This file expresses one stream and the game has two running at once -- these
hourly slots every day, PLUS the dated archboss slots at 17:00/20:00 on Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat. A day
with archbosses has both. Merging them is the next change; until it lands the timer shows only
what is in weeklySlots.
=== ARCHBOSS STREAM, supplied by the product owner 2026-08-06 for 07/08-25/08 ===
Cast is always the same five: Ramux, Ascended Giant Cordy, Ascended Deluzhnoa, Ascended Queen
Bellandir, Ascended Tevent. Structure is stable: Mon and Thu empty; Sun 18:00 castle siege (PvP,
weekly); Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat carry 17:00 and 20:00.
WHAT IS NOT DERIVABLE from three weeks, and must not be extrapolated:
- WHICH boss is guild on a given day. Sequenced by date it runs T, C, D, T, C, R, Q, R, T,
then TWO on 22/08 (D at 17:00 and R at 20:00), then Q. Both the one-per-day rule and any
clean rotation break at 22/08.
- WHETHER Ramux appears. It held to Wed+Sat for three weeks -- absent every Fri and on Tue
11/08 and 18/08 -- then appeared on Tue 25/08.
Three weeks cannot separate a longer cycle from server-side randomisation. So the archboss slots
need DATED entries refreshed per capture, not weekday ones with a guessed composition. Naming the
wrong contest is worse than naming none: a guildless player told a boss is open, or a guild told
it is theirs, both waste the trip.

fieldBosses.$comment: Roster from eventCalendar.getFieldBossEntries?input={"language":"en"}. Ids are questlog's; names are display names. Species tags are NOT in that payload and matter for advice — a boss's species pairs with the character sheet's Species tab, so 'swap to Demon damage before 21:00' becomes possible. Fill them in when captured.

bossRotation.$status: NOT CAPTURED. Which boss occupies each Field Boss slot on each weekday. Capture by opening each day on questlog's event calendar. Until filled, the timer announces the slot type ('Field Bosses') without naming the boss.

archBosses.$status: NOT CAPTURED. Arch bosses run a separate, less frequent schedule. Ramux arrived in 4.5.0 (Stillreach, two-phase with Atirat). A 'Boosted Arch Bosses' event ran 2026-07-28 to 2026-08-11 with four spawning simultaneously — note that limited-time events perturb the normal rotation, so the timer should support a temporary override rather than assuming the base table always holds.
